He is associated with Kufa, Damascus and Egypt, took part in the conquest of Damascus, fought at Siffin with Mu'awiya and at Marj Rahit with al-Dahhak ibn Qays, and died in 64 AH / 684 CE. Narrators from him include Abu al-Juwayriya al-Jarmi, Suhayl ibn Dhira' and 'Utba ibn Rafi'. The page cites Mu'jam al-Sahaba of Ibn Qani', Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba and al-Zirikli's al-A'lam.

bio: Abyad ibn Hammal al-Saba'i al-Mazini, of Ma'rib in Yemen, was a companion whose lineage Usd al-Ghaba gives on the authority of the genealogist al-Hamdani. His hadith is found in the collections of Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban. No death year is given. His son al-Harith ibn Bilal and 'Alqama ibn Waqqas narrated from him. The page cites al-Isti'ab, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba, Mu'jam al-Sahaba and al-A'lam.

bio: Al-Harith ibn al-Harith al-Ash'ari was a Syrian companion who narrated from the Prophet; Abu Sallam al-Aswad narrated from him. No death year is given.

He also narrated from Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari and Hudhayfa, and al-Aswad ibn Hilal narrated from him. bio: 'Abbad ibn Shayban al-Ansari al-Sulami is listed as a companion of the Prophet. Al-Mizzi in Tahdhib al-Kamal (14/127) states that both he and his father had companionship, and al-Dhahabi in al-Kashif (3/74) confirms his companionship. His sons Ibrahim and Abu Hubayra Yahya narrated from him. No death year or city is given.
research_evidence: عباد بن شيبان ... الأنصاري، السلمي ... له ولأبيه صحبة

bio: 'Abdullah ibn 'Adi ibn al-Hamra' al-Qurashi, an ally of Banu Zuhra from the Hijaz, was a companion who narrated from the Prophet. Al-Bukhari says he had companionship, was known by the kunya Abu 'Amr or Abu 'Umar, lived at Qudayd (between Qudayd and 'Usfan) and was among those who embraced Islam at the conquest of Mecca. Abu Hatim al-Razi also affirms his companionship. Abu Salama ibn 'Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im narrated from him. No death year is given.
research_evidence: له صحبة، يكنى أبا عمرو، وأبا عمر، وكان ينزل قديدا، وهو من مسلمة الفتح
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full_name_ar: عبد الرحمن بن عائش ( رضي الله عنه
bio: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'A'ish al-Hadrami (also said to be al-Saksaki), a Syrian narrator, is recorded as narrating from the Prophet (with dispute), from Mu'adh ibn Jabal and from Malik ibn Yukhamir; Khalid ibn al-Lajlaj and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated from him. Quoting Tahdhib al-Tahdhib (2/520), Abu Hatim al-Razi says he was a tabi'i and that whoever claimed companionship for him erred, while Ibn Khuzayma and al-Tirmidhi state he did not hear from the Prophet. No death year is given.
research_evidence: عبد الرحمن بن عائش ... هو تابعي، وأخطأ من قال: له صحبة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: Qurra bin Iyas al-Muzani was a companion who settled in Basra, where his house stood near al-'Awaqa. The page states that no one narrated from him except his son Mu'awiya bin Qurra, and that he was the grandfather of Iyas bin Mu'awiya, the judge of Basra. It gives his death as 64 AH (683 CE), citing al-Isti'ab, Usd al-Ghaba, Mu'jam al-Sahaba of Ibn Qani', al-Isaba and Mashahir 'Ulama' al-Amsar.
research_evidence: قرة بْن إِيَاس بْن رئاب الْمُزْنِيّ. سكن البصرة، وداره بها بحضرة العوقة. لم يرو عَنْهُ غير ابنه مُعَاوِيَة بْن قرة

full_name_ar: قطبة بن مالك الثعلبي ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Qutba bin Malik al-Tha'labi was a companion from Banu Tha'laba bin Dhubyan, which is why he is also called al-Dhubyani. He settled in Kufa and was the paternal uncle of Ziyad bin 'Alaqa, who narrated from him. The page compiles entries from Rijal Sahih Muslim, al-Isti'ab, Mu'jam al-Sahaba of Ibn Qani', Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba and Mashahir 'Ulama' al-Amsar; no death year is given.

bio: The page (headed Kathir bin al-Sa'ib al-Qurazi) compiles entries from Usd al-Ghaba and al-Isaba. It records a report, transmitted via 'Umara bin Khuzayma and cited to Ibn Manda, in which Kathir bin al-Sa'ib says the youths were presented before the Prophet on the day of Hunayn and those who had reached puberty were killed while the others were spared. Ibn Hibban is noted as listing him among the trustworthy Tabi'in; no death year is given.

bio: Al-Lajlaj al-'Amiri, of Banu 'Amir bin Sa'sa'a, is recorded as a companion whose narrations are mostly from Mu'adh bin Jabal. The page states he settled in Damascus and died at the age of 120, with accounts varying on his age at conversion. His sons al-'Ala' and Khalid narrated from him. Sources compiled include al-Isti'ab, Usd al-Ghaba, al-Isaba and Mashahir 'Ulama' al-Amsar; no death year is given.

bio: Abu Ma'bad Mujalid bin Mas'ud al-Sulami was a companion and the brother of Mujashi' bin Mas'ud. The page states he embraced Islam after the conquest of Mecca, settled in Basra, and is reported to have been killed at the Battle of the Camel in 36 AH (656 CE). Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi narrated from him. Sources compiled include Mu'jam al-Sahaba of Ibn Qani', Usd al-Ghaba, al-Tabaqat of Ibn Sa'd and al-Isaba.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 6635) lists Hilal, mawla of Rib'i bin Hirash, a Kufan. He narrated from his master Rib'i bin Hirash, and Abd al-Malik bin Umayr narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in Kitab al-Thiqat; al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah transmitted his narration without naming him.
research_evidence: هلال، مولى ربعي بن حراش، كوفي
dod_s: c. 753 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal lists al-Walid bin Abada (with fatha on the ba), the Egyptian mawla of Amr bin al-As and father of Amr bin al-Walid bin Abada. He narrated from Amr bin al-As and Abd Allah bin Amr, and Yazid bin Abi Habib narrated from him. The entry reports his death in the year 100 AH on the authority of al-Hasan bin Ali al-Addas, with another report giving 103 AH; Ibn Hajar in al-Taqrib graded him thiqa, though he was also described as majhul.
research_evidence: الوليد بن عبدة بفتح الباء والد عمرو بن الوليد بن عبدة المصري مولى عمرو بن العاص

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal lists Yahya bin al-Mukhtar al-San'ani, marked as a narrator of al-Nasa'i. He narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri; al-Hakam bin Zuhayr, Ma'mar bin Rashid and Yusuf bin Ya'qub al-Duba'i narrated from him. Al-Nasa'i recorded his hadith, and al-Mizzi notes the hadith reached him with a short chain.
research_evidence: س: يَحْيَى بن المختار الصنعاني رَوَى عَن: الْحَسَن البَصْرِيّ
dod_s: c. 753 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 7054) lists Yazid bin Miqsam al-Thaqafi, their mawla, of Ta'if, known as Yazid bin Dabba after his mother, and father of Abd Allah bin Yazid. He narrated from Maymuna bint Kardam; his son Abd Allah, his grandson Abd al-Azim bin Abd Allah, and Abd Allah bin Abd al-Rahman bin Ya'la al-Ta'ifi narrated from him. Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat; al-Bukhari (al-Adab and Af'al al-Ibad), Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah recorded his narrations. The entry notes he was a prolific, well-known poet who lived long enough to be met by al-Asma'i.
research_students: Abd Allah bin Yazid bin Miqsam

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal lists Abu Isra'il al-Jushami, whose name was Shu'ayb. He narrated from his master Ja'da al-Jushami, a Companion, and Shu'ba bin al-Hajjaj narrated from him. Ibn Hibban mentioned him in Kitab al-Thiqat, al-Nasa'i recorded his hadith in Amal al-Yawm wa-al-Layla, and Ibn Hajar graded him maqbul in al-Taqrib.
research_evidence: أبو إسرائيل الجشمي اسمه: شعيب

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal lists Abu Bishr, muezzin of the Damascus mosque, said to be from the people of Qinnasrin. He narrated from Amir bin Ludayn al-Ash'ari, Umar bin Abd al-Aziz and Makhul al-Shami; Rashid bin Sa'd, Sa'id bin Abd al-Aziz and Mu'awiya (bin Salih) narrated from him. The entry is marked as a narrator in Abu Dawud's al-Marasil.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal lists Abu al-Jarrah, mawla of Umm Habiba, wife of the Prophet; some said his name was al-Zubayr, and some narrators call him al-Jarrah. Ibn Hibban listed him in al-Thiqat and Ibn Hajar graded him maqbul; Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i recorded his hadith.

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 7376) lists Abu Zayd, mawla of Banu Tha'laba, whose name is said to be al-Walid. Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah recorded his hadith on the prohibition of facing the qibla when relieving oneself; Abu Zur'a said he was unknown.

bio: Wikipedia describes Zufar ibn al-Hudhayl, known as Imam Zufar, as an 8th-century scholar born in Isfahan in 110 or 111 AH during his father's governorship there, a leading member of Abu Hanifa's circle and the fourth imam of the Hanafi school, who spread Hanafi jurisprudence in Basra. His teachers included al-A'mash, Yahya bin Sa'id al-Ansari, Ibn Ishaq, Isma'il bin Abi Khalid and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani; his students included Muhammad al-Shaybani, Uthman al-Batti, Shaddad bin Hakim and Abu Wahb Muhammad bin Muzahim. He died in Basra in 158 AH (775 CE). Works attributed to him include al-Athar (narrations from Abu Hanifa) and two hadith booklets.
research_evidence: Zufar died in Basra in 158 AH (775 CE) and was buried there.

bio: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Yazid, Abu Muhammad al-Makki al-Muqri', was a Meccan Quran reciter and hadith narrator of the ninth tabaqa. According to the hdith.com card he narrated from Ibn Jurayj, and reciters such as Ahmad al-Bazzi and Hamid bin Yahya al-Balkhi transmitted his Quran reading. Al-Khalili called him trustworthy, while al-'Uqayli said his hadith is not corroborated; Ibn Hajar graded him maqbul and al-Dhahabi said he is not a proof (ghayr hujja). His death is dated only to the range 201-211 AH; twelve narrations are attributed to him.

full: Thabit bin (Yazid bin) Wadi'a b. Kudham b. Khalid b. Tha'laba b. Zayd b. 'Ubaid b. Zayd b. Malik
full_name_ar: ثابت بن وديعة الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 834, symbols د س ق) gives him as Thabit ibn Wadi'a, also said to be Thabit ibn Yazid ibn Wadi'a or Thabit ibn Zayd ibn Wadi'a, al-Ansari, kunya Abu Sa'id. He narrated from the Prophet; al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, Zayd ibn Wahb al-Juhani and 'Amir ibn Sa'd al-Bajali narrated from him. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah record a single hadith from him. The entry notes scholarly disagreement over whether the name variants refer to one person. No death year is given.
research_evidence: ثابت بن وديعة، ويُقال: ثابت بْن يزيد بْن وديعة، ويُقال: ثابت بْن زيد بْن وديعة
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Thabit bin Al-Samit b. 'Ady b. Ka'b b. 'Abdul Ashhal
full_name_ar: ثابت بن الصامت الأنصاري الأشهلي ( رضي الله عنه

possible_duplicate_of.core_famous: Umm Thabit bint Mas'ud b. Sa'd

bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal (entry 818, symbol ق for Ibn Majah) gives him as Thabit ibn al-Samit al-Ansari al-Ashhali, father of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn al-Samit, and said to be the brother of 'Ubada ibn al-Samit. He is counted among the companions, though the entry notes disagreement, and has one hadith with a disputed chain, about the Prophet praying among Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal wearing a cloak, recorded by Ibn Majah. No death year is given.

full: Khadij bin Rafi' bin 'Adi b. Zayd b. Jushum b. Haritha b. al-Harith b. al-Khazraj
full_name_ar: خديج بن رافع بن عدي الأنصاري ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal lists Khadij ibn Rafi' ibn 'Adi, father of Rafi' ibn Khadij, under the section on errors (al-awham). Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim (Ibn 'Asakir) had noted a hadith attributed to Khadij on the prohibition of leasing land for sharecropping, transmitted via 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazri from Mujahid; al-Mizzi states that Khadij is not known to have companionship, let alone narration, and that the attribution arose from a copyist's error rather than from the original narrator, the hadith being properly Rafi' ibn Khadij's. No dates are given.
research_evidence: خديج بْن رافع بن عدي، والد رافع بْن خديج
dod_s: c. 680 CE (estimated from generation — no recorded date survives)

full: Zuhayr bin Rafi' bin 'Adi b. Zayd b. Jushum b. Haritha b. al-Harith b. al-Khazraj
full_name_ar: ظهير بن رافع ( رضي الله عنه
bio: Tahdhib al-Kamal gives him as Zuhayr ibn Rafi' ibn 'Adi ibn Zayd ibn Jusham ibn Haritha, al-Ansari al-Awsi al-Harithi, of Medina, paternal uncle of Rafi' ibn Khadij, and a companion. He witnessed the second 'Aqaba pledge; his presence at Badr is disputed. He narrated from the Prophet, and his nephew Rafi' ibn Khadij narrated from him. Al-Bukhari, Muslim, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah record a single hadith from him, on the Prophet's prohibition of a form of leasing farmland. No death year is given.
research_evidence: ظهير بن رافع بن عدي بن زيد بن جشم بن حارثة بن الحارث بن عَمْرو بن مالك بن الأوس الأَنْصارِيّ، الأوسي، الحارثي، المدني، عم رافع بن خديج، له صحبة
